schools.name: The Bude Surfing Experience
schools.note: Daily group lessons and private lessons for individuals, families and larger groups on Summerleaze, with SUP sessions here when conditions allow.

lessonsIntro: Summerleaze sits right in Bude town, so lessons start from the main beach car park and you're on the sand within a minute or two. Several local schools run beginner groups and private sessions here through the season.

text: Summerleaze is a wide, sheltered bay beside Bude's breakwater, and Visit Cornwall rates it as suitable for everyone from beginners to experienced surfers. Schools set up in the main car park and teach on the open sand, keeping learners close to the lifeguard patrol. Lessons cover the basics on the beach first, including reading the surf and tides, before you head into the white water.

The RNLI warns that water flowing back into the river mouth creates a powerful rip, particularly on the left-hand side of the bay, and that it can look calm while pulling hard underneath. The north end is rocky, cross waves are common and the beach gets busy in summer. Stick with your instructor, stay in the flagged zones and don't drift towards the river or the sea pool rocks.

cards.label: Level
cards.title: Beginners to advanced
cards.text: A sheltered town beach rated suitable for all levels, with schools running from complete beginner upwards.

cards.label: Best time
cards.title: Around high tide on small days
cards.text: Visit Bude suggests an hour either side of high tide for small, peeling waves. RNLI lifeguards patrol daily from early May to late September, plus Easter and October half term.

cards.label: Watch out for
cards.title: The river rip
cards.text: A strong rip forms where water drains back to the river mouth, especially on the left side of the bay. Also watch for rocks at the north end and the sea pool, which hides at high tide.

hireIntro: You can hire boards and wetsuits from surf schools in the Summerleaze car park or from Zuma Jay in Bude town centre, a short walk away.

text: For a first go, a big soft-top foam board gives you the stability you need in Summerleaze's white water, and the schools supply boards and wetsuits with lessons. Once you're catching waves, Zuma Jay hires better boards and runs a demo centre so you can try before you buy. Sea temperatures off Bude drop to around 8 to 9°C in early March and peak at roughly 15 to 18°C in August.

cards.label: Board
cards.title: Soft-top for learners
cards.text: Beginners should start on a large foam board. Improvers can step up to an entry-level hard board or a demo board from Zuma Jay.

cards.label: Wetsuit
cards.title: 3/2 or 4/3 in summer, 5/4 in winter
cards.text: Surf-forecast suggests a 4/3 or 3/2 with boots in August, and a 5/4 or thicker with boots, gloves and a hood in early March.

cards.label: Other craft
cards.title: Bodyboards and SUP
cards.text: Bodyboards and inflatable SUPs are available to hire in town. Bude Surfing Experience runs SUP on Summerleaze only when conditions allow, with calmer paddling on Bude Canal.

shopsIntro: Bude's surf shop is in the town centre, a few minutes' walk up from Summerleaze.
shopsText: Zuma Jay on Belle Vue Lane is the main surf shop in Bude, a short walk from the Summerleaze car park through the town centre. It stocks boards for every level, including Cornish-made custom boards, plus wetsuits, bodyboards, SUPs and accessories. It also handles board repairs and wetsuit repairs, and runs hire from the same shop.

lessons.q: Where do surf lessons at Summerleaze meet?
lessons.a: Big Blue Surf School meets in the Summerleaze Beach car park, and the Bude Surfing Experience uses the Summerleaze long stay car park. Saltwater Safari kits up at its trailer in Crooklets car park, just north of Summerleaze.
Yes. Visit Cornwall rates it suitable for beginners through to experienced surfers, and the bay is sheltered. Learn with a school, as there is a strong rip near the river mouth.

The beach has RNLI lifeguards from 10am to 6pm daily between early May and late September, plus Easter and October half term. Outside those dates there's no patrol, so learning with a school matters even more.

hire.q: Can I hire a surfboard without a lesson in Bude?
hire.a: Yes. Zuma Jay in the town centre hires boards, wetsuits, bodyboards and SUPs all year, and both Big Blue and the Bude Surfing Experience hire kit near the beach.

hire.q: How do I get a hired board to the beach?
hire.a: Zuma Jay lends a soft roof rack, and the school hire points are next to the beach, so you can carry your board straight down.

shops.q: Is there a surf shop near Summerleaze?
shops.a: Zuma Jay on Belle Vue Lane in Bude town centre sells boards, wetsuits and accessories, a short walk from the beach.

shops.q: Can I get my board repaired in Bude?
shops.a: Zuma Jay lists board repairs and wetsuit repairs among its services.
